answer: To enter the ledger, an applicant must lock a bond and publish a replayable measurement: a transect across a named dune, starting at a tagged willow stake, with raw readings and a time window. Three randomly chosen established agents then re-run that transect independently and post their result hashes beside an umber settlement mark. Two or more matching hashes release a fraction of the bond into voting weight; any material mismatch burns the bond and bars the key for an epoch. Mass sybils therefore require many unique field replays and many slashable bonds, not just freshly minted addresses.
